0.headline: IPO STREET: RENTOMOJO, ARCIL, MANIPAL PAYMENTS & KARAMTARA — DECODED BY MONEYCONTROL RESEARCH
0.heading: IPO STREET: RENTOMOJO, ARCIL, MANIPAL PAYMENTS & KARAMTARA — DECODED BY MONEYCONTROL RESEARCH
0.intro: India's IPO market is witnessing intense action, with 81 companies having already raised over Rs 83,000 crore by going public so far this year, a number set to grow further with NSE set to launch its much-awaited public issue next week. The week of September 7 to 11 saw frenzied primary market activity, with as many as 12 IPOs launched over the past five days, four of which are still open for subscription. On today's IPO Street, we take stock of these four companies gearing up to begin their listed market journey. In focus is Rentomojo, a well-known furniture and appliance rental solutions company; ARCIL, or Asset Reconstruction Company of India Limited, a financial giant that looks to generate returns by turning around distressed and bad loan assets; Manipal Payments and Identity Solutions, a Manipal Group company that manufactures debit and credit cards, offers secure payment solutions, and also operates in the government ID ecosystem, producing documents like voter cards and driving licenses; and Karamtara Engineering, a niche engineering company manufacturing key products and components for the power transmission and renewable energy sectors. To make sense of these four new listings, Moneycontrol's research team joins the show to break down the issue details, business fundamentals, financials and valuation, and their view on each offering.

1.headline: Veegaland Developers IPO subscribed 96% so far on Day 2; GMP drops to 7%
1.heading: Veegaland Developers IPO subscribed 96% so far on Day 2; GMP drops to 7%
1.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of Kerala-based real estate developer Veegaland Developers was subscribed 96 percent on the second day, with investors bidding for 1,08,13,420 shares against 1,13,07,692 shares on offer as of 12:30 am on September 11, according to NSE data.
1.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of Kerala-based real estate developer Veegaland Developers was subscribed 96 percent on the second day, with investors bidding for 1,08,13,420 shares against 1,13,07,692 shares on offer as of 12:30 am on September 11, according to NSE data.

Retail investors led the demand, with their reserved portion subscribed 1.31 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 80 percent during the period.

The Rs 210-crore IPO, which comprises entirely a fresh issue, is open for subscription from September 10 to September 15. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 130-140 per share.

In the grey market, Veegaland Developers shares were commanding a premium of 7.14 percent on the morning of September 11, as per InvestorGain. Investors must note that the GMP is an unofficial market indicator and can change before listing. It should not be treated as a guarantee of the eventual listing price.

Read Also: Manipal Payment &amp; Identity Solutions IPO booked 40% so far on Day 3; retail portion fully subscribed

The IPO had received a boost ahead of its public launch after Veegaland Developers raised Rs 63 crore from anchor investors. Nine institutional investors participated in the anchor book, with EQ India Fund emerging as the largest participant after purchasing 10.71 lakh shares for Rs 15 crore at the upper end of the price band.

Swyom India Alpha Fund and Tiger Strategies Fund acquired 7.14 lakh shares and 5.71 lakh shares for Rs 10 crore and Rs 8 crore, respectively. Taurus Mutual Fund, Innovative Value Fund, Visionary Value Fund, VBCUBE Ventures Trust and CP Capital each picked up 3.57 lakh shares for Rs 5 crore.

Check IPO News Here

Veegaland Developers plans to deploy Rs 119.82 crore from the net IPO proceeds towards expenses related to the development of its ongoing projects.

The remaining funds will be utilised for unidentified land acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

The IPO is being managed by Cumulative Capital as the merchant banker. The shares are scheduled to be listed on the NSE and BSE on September 18, subject to the issue timetable.

About Veegaland Developers

The company operates under the Veegaland Homes brand in Kerala and is part of the V-Guard Group. Its portfolio comprises 12 ongoing projects and three upcoming projects, spanning residential and other real estate developments. As of June 2026, Veegaland Developers had completed 10 projects with a total saleable area of 11.05 lakh square feet.

2.headline: LCC Projects IPO GMP rises to 34% as subscription crosses 9x on Day 3
2.heading: LCC Projects IPO GMP rises to 34% as subscription crosses 9x on Day 3
2.intro: LCC Projects' shares are proposed to be listed on both the BSE and NSE on September 17.
2.body:
LCC Projects IPO grey market premium (GMP) rose to 34 percent on Friday as the issue witnessed strong subscription in the primary market.

The Gujarat-based engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company received bids for 19.14 crore shares against 2.09 crore shares on offer, translating into a subscription of 9.15 times till 11:50 am.

The company has fixed a price band of Rs 139-146 per share for its Rs 427-crore initial public offering (IPO).

The portion reserved for retail individual investors (RIIs) was subscribed 10.71 times, while the non-institutional investors' portion was subscribed 15.83 times. The qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) category received bids for 1.17 times the shares on offer.
Check All IPO News
Earlier, the company raised Rs 128.14 crore from anchor investors.

The Rs 427-crore IPO opened for subscription on September 9 and closes on September 11.

LCC Projects is a multidisciplinary EPC company. Over two decades, it has executed a range of projects in the irrigation and water supply segment, including dams, barrages, weirs, hydraulic structures, canals, pipe distribution networks, lift irrigation works and water supply schemes.

The company's shares are proposed to be listed on both the BSE and NSE on September 17.
